title: Benchmark submission
description: One machine's measurements, contributed to the aggregate. A submission carries at least two tools measured under the same conditions, because it is the ratio between them that travels — never the seconds.

conditions.description: What the aggregate uses to decide whether a submission is trustworthy enough to weight normally.

maxForeignCpuPercent.description: Highest background load, excluding the tool being measured, seen during any scoring run.

loadSpreadPercentagePoints.description: Difference in background load between the busiest and quietest tool's leg. Large values mean the tools were not measured under the same conditions.

driftRatio.description: Closing control divided by opening control. 1.00 means the machine did not change underneath the run.

remoteDesktopActive.description: Screen sharing encodes through the same hardware H.264 block the exports use; submissions with this true are down-weighted.

step.description: Which rung of the ladder. Only tools measured on the same rung may be compared.

downloadSha256.description: Required for public-bundle: it is what proves two machines measured the same footage.

measurements.description: At least two tools. One tool contributes no ratio and cannot join the graph; no particular tool is required.

localFloorMs.description: Floor measured beside this tool. Present, it is what makes the submission comparable across machines.

softwareFloorMs.description: The same clip encoded with libx264, bound by the cores rather than the fixed-function block the hardware floor uses. The two do not throttle together, so their ratio says how much a cost figure owes to this machine's encoder rather than to the tool.

outputMeanVolumeDb.description: A silent track passes every check that only asks whether audio exists.

contradicted.description: Features the tool reported as configured but the pixel verifier could not find in the output.

verified.description: Output passed metadata, pixel and audio verification. Unverified measurements are recorded and excluded from the ratio graph.
